newsitem.title: USA: Hummer maker AM General says eyes cost cuts.
newsitem.headline: Hummer maker AM General says eyes cost cuts.

text.p: AM General Corp., the company that makes the Hummer military vehicle, said it is reviewing plans to cut overhead costs and produce fewer vehicles.
AM General reported Thursday that it lost $19.6 million in its fiscal year ended Oct. 31, compared with a loss of $3.5 million the previous year.
The company also said Paul Schuchman, its chief financial officer, resigned earlier this month. His duties will be assumed temporarily by Chief Executive Officer James Armour, the company said.
A spokesman declined to elaborate on cost-cutting plans.

AM General has sold about 140,000 Hummers since the wide-body, go-anywhere vehicle debuted in 1984. Hollywood actor Arnold Schwarzenegger owns one. So do techno-thriller author Tom Clancy and boxer Mike Tyson.
Commercial sales of the Hummer continue to grow, but remain a tiny fraction of the company's business, which is dominated by military procurement, the spokesman said.

In reporting its loss Thursday, AM General said fiscal 1996 sales were $462.4 million compared with $411.7 million a year earlier. Profits were hurt by postponement of $25.4 million in foreign sales involving 768 vehicles, the company said.

"In October, 167 vehicles were delivered, and subsequent to fiscal year-end an additional 120 vehicles have been delivered. Delivery of the balance is now anticipated in the first half of fiscal 1997," the company said.
AM General is controlled by The Renco Group, a New York investment company.
